chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from Hishām ibn Sālim, from Abī Baṣīr, who said:
I asked Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام about a mudabbar slave who killed a man intentionally. He said: “He is to be killed for him.”

He said: I said: Then if he killed him by mistake? He said: “He is handed over to the heirs of the slain, and he becomes theirs. If they wish, they may enslave him, and they have no right to kill him.”
He said: Then he said: “O Abā Muḥammad, indeed the mudabbar remains owned.”

key_terms.أَوْلِيَاءِ الْمَقْتُولِ: the legal heirs of the person who was killed
key_terms.اسْتَرَقُّوهُ: they take him as a slave
key_terms.مُدَبَّرٍ: a slave promised freedom upon the master's death

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a mudabbar slave who kills someone intentionally or by mistake in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding a mudabbar slave who kills another person. If the killing is intentional, qiṣāṣ applies; if it is accidental, he is handed over to the heirs of the victim, who may keep him as a slave but may not kill him. The Imam عليه السلام concludes by affirming that a mudabbar still remains legally a mamlūk.
